_comment: Lifecycle configuration for the OFFSITE BACKUP bucket only (not the three media buckets in r2-setup.md).
THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO EXPIRATION RULE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS FILE.
docs/BACKUP-RECOVERY.md section 2 has the reasoning. Short version: retention lives in
scripts/dr/backup-lib.mjs keysToPrune, which never prunes below the newest 7 backups whatever
their age. A bucket lifecycle Expiration rule has no such floor. Add `Expiration: {Days: 30}`
here and the day the dump job stops running becomes the day a 30-day timer starts on the last
backup that exists, with nothing writing new ones and nothing reporting it. The two mechanisms
look interchangeable and are not: one degrades to 'kept too much', the other to 'kept nothing'.
R2 HAS NO OBJECT VERSIONING AND NO OBJECT LOCK. Measured 2026-09-10 against Cloudflare's own
S3 compatibility matrix: PutBucketVersioning and GetBucketVersioning are listed unimplemented,
ListObjectVersions is absent, and x-amz-object-lock-* are unsupported on every object operation.
The substitute for versioning is that backup keys are immutable by construction: every dump is
named for the UTC minute it was taken, so a write can never overwrite a previous backup.
